correctness: Body validity is keyed only to explicitly declared canonical source domains.
Path-only mutation increments metadata revision only.
Same-width import mutation increments imports and content-hash revisions only.
Unknown body/domain binding is invalidated instead of guessed valid.
Positional workspace reorder is now visible to all positional domain identities.
Every benchmark output is bound to a precomputed fresh direct-baseline result hash.
strongestSupportedClaim: Versioned canonical domain identities and per-body validity keys can preserve derived bodies across unrelated whole-state changes while retaining exact outputs. In the current 2,500-file harness this materially reduces cache execution and reconstruction, but the naive full-scan construction of all domain identities is expensive enough to erase the measured runtime advantage when charged synchronously.
boundaries: Does not prove domain identity construction is cheap.
Does not prove end-to-end speedup with the current full-scan identity builder.
Does not prove automatic semantic dependency inference.
Does not prove production-scale superiority or global cache optimality.
Five hosted samples reduce single-run noise but are not a broad statistical performance distribution.
No created RAM, free compute, free energy, or universal speedup claim.
nextGate: Replace full-scan domain identity construction with deterministic incremental domain revision updates driven by trusted canonical mutation/transition receipts. Measure receipt/update cost against whole-state hashing and prove unchanged domain hashes do not need rescanning.
